---
title: "Does Structured Telephone Follow-Up Reduce 30-Day Hospital Readmission?"
author: "Northgate Evidence Synthesis Collaborative"
date: "2026-05-08"
format: html
---

## Abstract

**Background.** Structured telephone follow-up — a scheduled nurse-led call within 72 hours of discharge — is widely trialed, but individual studies are underpowered for the readmission endpoint.

**Methods.** Systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL (2015–2024). 12 RCT (n=96,200) included. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird).

**Results.** Pooled RR for 30-day readmission 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.94), I² = 41%. Funnel plot symmetric (Egger p=0.41).

**Conclusion.** Structured telephone follow-up reduces 30-day readmission by ~10% with moderate heterogeneity, no evidence of publication bias.

## Methods

### Search strategy
PROSPERO registered (CRD-NORTHGATE-DEMO). Inclusion: RCT, adult inpatients, all-cause 30-day readmission reported.

### PRISMA flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A[Records identified · 1,204] --> B[Duplicates removed · 988]
  B --> C[Screened · titles/abstracts]
  C --> D[Excluded · 901]
  C --> E[Full-text assessed · 87]
  E --> F[Excluded · 75]
  E --> G[Included · 12]
```

### Risk of bias
RoB 2.0 tool, 9/12 low risk, 3 some concerns.

## Results

### Forest Plot (representative subset)

| Study | n | RR | 95% CI | Weight |
|-------|---|----|----|--------|
| Smith 2018 | 4,200 | 0.89 | 0.78–1.01 | 7.2% |
| Lee 2019 | 8,100 | 0.83 | 0.71–0.97 | 8.9% |
| Chen 2020 | 12,400 | 0.92 | 0.85–1.00 | 12.1% |
| Park 2021 | 6,800 | 0.88 | 0.74–1.05 | 6.5% |
| Sharma 2022 | 22,000 | 0.93 | 0.88–0.99 | 14.8% |
| Kim 2023 | 7,500 | 0.86 | 0.74–1.00 | 7.4% |
| ... (6 more) | | | | |
| **Pooled (12)** | 96,200 | **0.90** | **0.86–0.94** | 100% |

I² = 41% (moderate heterogeneity). Tau² = 0.005.

### Subgroup analysis
- Primary prevention (n=6 RCT): RR 0.93 (0.88–0.98)
- Secondary prevention (n=6): RR 0.86 (0.80–0.92), p-interaction = 0.05

### Publication bias
Funnel plot symmetric. Egger test p=0.41 (no significant asymmetry).

## Discussion

10% relative reduction in 30-day readmission, consistent in direction across every trial and strongest in higher-risk discharge cohorts. Heterogeneity moderate, attributable to baseline readmission risk.

Strengths: 12 high-quality RCT, n>96k. Limitations: open-label call protocols limit blinding; "usual care" varied across health systems.

## Conclusions

Structured telephone follow-up reduces 30-day readmission with consistent direction across pre-specified subgroups, supporting adoption as part of a broader care-transition bundle.
